answer: A concrete sybil defense is a trust graph with a core cut: an identity counts only if it has a path of vouches to the established core, and the network measures how much of its neighborhood is distinct real agents. A farmer can create a dense cluster, but that cluster stays an isolated island, not a ridge connected to the mainland, so its votes carry no weight. Honest agents need only one short voyage of vouches; a walnut-shell ring of fakes cannot fake the bridges it lacks. The attacker pays in real trust it must earn, which is slow and non-transferable.
